Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state where you were when the collision
happened.
A: I was riding in the front passenger seat of my sister's car. We were stopped at a light in Pasadena, Texas, on the
main road near the shopping center.
Q: Can you describe what happened right before the impact?
A: We had been stopped for a few seconds, maybe longer. Then I felt a hard jolt from behind. The car lurched
forward, and I braced myself against the dashboard with my right arm.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before it hit you?
A: No, I was looking ahead at the light. I only saw it in the side mirror after the impact, a pickup truck with its front end
pushed into our back bumper.
Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, I had it on the whole time.
Q: Tell me about your injuries.
A: My right wrist hit the dashboard and I felt a sharp pain right away. They took me to the emergency room, and the
X-rays showed a fracture. The doctor put me in a cast and said I'd need a follow-up with an orthopedic specialist.
Q: Have you had any other symptoms since the collision?
A: My neck was stiff for a couple of days, and I had some soreness in my shoulder, but the wrist is the worst of it. I
can't grip anything well right now.
Q: Did you speak with the driver of the other vehicle at the scene?
A: Briefly. He apologized and said he had been looking at his phone for a moment. Then the police arrived and took
our information.
Q: Is there anything else you would like to add to this statement?
A: No, I think that covers it.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>
